references.text: The parallel text in Matthew's account of the temptation, where the devil takes Jesus to the pinnacle of the temple in Jerusalem and challenges him to throw himself down, saying, "Are you the Son of God".
Earlier in the temptation narrative, the devil uses the same phrasing, "Are you the Son of God" (Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ), to tempt Jesus, showing a consistent pattern in the temptations.
Later in the same chapter, the crowd in Nazareth tries to throw Jesus off a cliff, which thematically recalls the devil's challenge to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

The temple in Jerusalem and its holiness are central to this temptation. Solomon's temple is described here as God's dwelling place, and the pinnacle of the temple (πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ) is where the temptation takes place.

Psalm 91:11–12 is the scripture the devil quotes in the next verse (Luke 4:10–11) as justification for why Jesus can safely throw himself down from the pinnacle of the temple, since angels will carry him.
Jerusalem and the temple are already linked to Jesus' identity from childhood. His parents brought him to the temple, and it is here that the devil now challenges his divinity.
Matthew uses the same expression, "Are you the Son of God," in the first temptation, showing that this is the devil's repeated strategy to challenge Jesus' identity and obedience to the Father.
